lines.text: Learning about working in the Netherlands.
Are you a person going through civic integration [inburgeraar]?
Then you must take several exams: exams for the Dutch language and for knowledge of Dutch society [KNM, kennis van de Nederlandse maatschappij].
You must also do the labour market and participation module [MAP, module arbeidsmarkt en participatie].
In the labour market part you learn: which jobs exist, which jobs are suitable [geschikt] for you, and how to apply for a job [solliciteren].
You must also do practical assignments [praktijkopdrachten], for example volunteer work [vrijwilligerswerk], an internship [stage] or paid work.
Are you not an inburgeraar?
Then you can take courses, for example at the municipality.
Who provides your income?
Did you come to the Netherlands because you have a partner here?
Then your partner may provide your income [inkomen] at first.
But in principle you are responsible for your own income.
In special situations you can get a benefit payment [uitkering], but there are strict requirements [eisen] for that.
Finding a job through your network.
Many people find a job through their own network [netwerk].
They know people inside a company where there is a job opening [vacature], or they hear from others that there is a vacancy somewhere.
That is why it is important to have a network in the Netherlands, and to let that network know what kind of work you are looking for.
You can also build up [opbouwen] a network through volunteer work.
Finding vacancies online.
There are also online networks, for example LinkedIn.
Through such a network you can sometimes find work.
There are also other websites with vacancies.
You can search by the type of work or position/role [functie] and the place where you are looking for work.
Temp agencies.
A temp agency [uitzendbureau] is a kind of marketplace for temporary [tijdelijk] work.
It helps companies find people, so it can also find work for you.
The temp agency is then actually your employer [werkgever].
You must first register [inschrijven] via the website.
After that you can get an interview and they look for work for you.
What do you need to send for a job application?
The employer must receive information about you.
Often you fill in an online application form [sollicitatieformulier], or you write an application/cover letter [sollicitatiebrief].
You must also always send your CV (curriculum vitae).
In your CV you write all your personal details [gegevens], your education and your work experience [werkervaring].
Preparing for a job interview.
Does the vacancy perhaps suit you?
Then you get an invitation [uitnodiging] to a job interview [sollicitatiegesprek].
You should prepare well for such an interview: then you have a bigger chance of getting the job.
You can look up information about the company and the position.
Asking questions.
The employer gets a good impression [indruk] of you if you ask questions yourself.
It shows that you are really interested [geïnteresseerd].
The questions can be about the company and the position, and about the employment conditions [arbeidsvoorwaarden]: for example your salary, working hours and holidays.
